_comment: Every learner-facing Korean string, with a hash of the text that was read. A string whose hash no longer matches has changed since its last reading and must be read again. Generated by scripts/build-copy-ledger.mjs; the decisions are written by the person reading.

common:report.field.category.why: 문제 alone reads as "question" as readily as "problem"

common:exit.title.why: 한귤 가나다를 닫을까요? named the product where the learner is already inside it; 앱을 종료할까요? is the sentence a phone asks

common:exit.stay.why: 계속하기 answered a question about leaving with a word about studying; 취소 is the answer to a dialog

common:exit.leave.why: 닫기 is what a window does; 종료 is what an app does

errors:generic.why: a question written with a full stop

home:celebrate.why: generic praise appended to a fact — "Lovely work." said nothing the sentence before it had not

home:finished.cta.why: a button that repeated the label above it word for word instead of naming an action

learning:review.prompt.distinguish.why: 어느 쪽 — the vague subject the copy rules forbid

learning:review.markWrong.why: a screen-reader label that read like a field dump

learning:units.unit-11.points[2].why: an unsupported claim about learners — "this is where most beginners’ reading breaks"

learning:recognition.question.why: The letter lesson asked “이 소리를 내는 글자는?” and review asked the same question in fuller words. One wording for one question.

learning:sounds.blurb.why: a question written with a full stop

learning:mistakes.times_other.why: 틀림 is a nominalisation; every sentence around it is 해요체

levelTest:intro.usedFor.why: 추천해 드려요 raised the honorific above the app’s own register

levelTest:home.cta.why: “레벨 테스트” and “레벨 테스트 하기” were one English sentence written two ways; the two buttons do the same thing and now say the same thing.

levelTest:placement.body.why: same honorific slip, and two sentences where one carries the fact

numbers:systemSino.why: “일, 이, 삼” was the set’s only name, so every question about it had to point at it. Named 한자어식.

numbers:systemNative.why: As systemSino: named 고유어식 rather than pointed at.

numbers:system.native.why: An answer option that did not say which set it was; now it names 고유어식.

numbers:action.retryMastery.why: “마무리 확인 다시 하기” restated the phase the screen was already in; the button is 다시 풀기.

numbers:action.backToCourse.why: 과정 is not the word the app uses for a lesson list; 수업.

numbers:practiceIntro.why: “필요한 곳에는 설명이 따라와요” promised a sentence the result state no longer draws.

numbers:masteryIntro.why: Told a learner a percentage and left them to do the arithmetic. Now a count: 10문제 중 8문제.

numbers:masteryPassed.why: “마무리 확인 통과 — 10문제 중 8개” is a fragment and a unit nobody speaks; a sentence with the score in it.

numbers:masteryFailed.why: “아직이에요” did not say what would be enough. It now gives the score and the mark.

numbers:masteryPerfect.why: Made consistent with masteryPassed, which now says it passed before saying the score.

numbers:summaryComplete.why: “수업 완료” is a label; the screen is telling a learner something.

numbers:summaryIncomplete.why: “아직 끝나지 않았어요” restated the state the list under it enumerates.

numbers:summaryMissing.mastery.why: “마무리 확인 통과하기” was drawn under a line already saying the check was failed and by how much.

numbers:feedback.incorrect.why: 조금 달라요 — "it is a little different" — softened a verdict the screen had already delivered in red, leaving a learner to work out whether it counted. 틀렸어요 is the answer to the question they asked

numbers:prompt.chooseSystem.why: “어떤 숫자를 쓸까요?” named neither of the two things being chosen between.

numbers:prompt.digitsToKorean.sino.why: “이 숫자를 일, 이, 삼으로 말해 보세요” pointed at both the numeral and the set; the numeral is already on the screen.

numbers:prompt.counterForm.why: carried 을(를) and 로 on a slot a template cannot pick a particle for

numbers:prompt.orderParts.why: 순서대로 눌러서 {{value}}을(를) 만들어 보세요 — the 은(는) parenthesis this product removed on purpose, and the one place still writing one. The digit cannot be given a particle by josa (35 is 삼십오 and takes 를; 20 is 이십 and takes 을), so the sentence was rebuilt to put the number first and not need one.

numbers:module.systems.title.why: “1부터 10까지 말해요” did not say the module is about two ways of doing it.

numbers:module.systems.goal.why: “0을 읽고, 어디에 어떤 말을 쓰는지도 익혀요” — 어떤 말 names nothing.

numbers:lesson.sinoBasics.title.why: “1, 2, 3을 한국어로 말해요” describes every lesson in the module.

numbers:lesson.sinoBasics.objective.why: Follows the retitled lesson and names the set.

numbers:lesson.sinoBasics.step1.why: Introduces the name 한자어식 수 표현 before the lesson asks a question about it.

numbers:lesson.sinoBasics.step2.why: Rewritten to carry the uses the first step could not hold: floors, addresses, measurements, large numbers.

numbers:lesson.sinoBasics.step3.why: Absorbed the worked examples the old step 3 held on its own.

numbers:lesson.nativeBasics.step1.why: Introduces the name 고유어식 수 표현.

numbers:lesson.nativeBasics.step2.why: Took the hundred-and-up rule from the old step 3.

numbers:lesson.nativeBasics.step3.why: Now teaches the counting forms explicitly: 하나 → 한 개, 스물 → 스무 개.

numbers:lesson.choosing.title.why: Named the two sets rather than listing their first members twice.

numbers:lesson.choosing.objective.why: Said “어떤 숫자” where it means one of two named things.

numbers:lesson.choosing.step1.why: Uses the name instead of repeating 하나, 둘, 셋.

numbers:lesson.choosing.step3.why: Says which half of the clock time is which set.

numbers:lesson.sinoBuild.step1.why: carried three worked examples, three arabic numerals and three hyphenated pseudo-spellings — 십일은 십-일, 11 — in one paragraph. 십-일 is not how the word is written, spoken or spelled. The examples are drawn now and the sentence is a caption on them

numbers:lesson.nativeBuild.objective.why: “하나, 둘, 셋 쪽” — 쪽 is the vague subject the copy rules forbid.

numbers:lesson.nativeBuild.step1.why: the same paragraph shape, one lesson over: the worked examples moved into the drawing and the sentence keeps only the rule

numbers:lesson.dates.step3.why: wrote 삼월 일 일 in the very sentence explaining that 일 is both

numbers:gloss.counterAge.why: An answer that named the set by listing it; it names it.

numbers:gloss.mixedTime.why: "시와 분이 같이 있는 시각"은 시각이 아니라 형식을 설명하는 말이라, 실제 시각들 사이에 놓이면 혼자 종류가 달랐다. 3시 30분으로 바꿨다.

numbers:gloss.monday.why: 한 주의 첫날 — contestable, and it is the correct answer to a question. Korean calendars start on Sunday, so a reader who counts from one finds Monday second. 한 주가 시작되는 날 says the thing nobody argues with.

numbers:gloss.friday.why: 한 주의 다섯째 날 — the same fault and worse: Friday is the fifth day counting from Monday and the sixth counting from Sunday, which is how a Korean calendar prints it. The correct answer looked wrong. 주말 바로 앞의 날 is relational and true either way.

settings:backup.body.why: ended with 어디에도 올라가지 않아요 — an implementation detail phrased as a privacy claim, on a screen that is not about privacy. The claim stays where it can be supported, on the Privacy screen

vocabulary:today.doneBlurb.why: generic praise, and 잘하셨어요 raised the honorific above the app’s own 해요체

vocabulary:saved.notPractisable.why: internal terminology: a learner has never met a "학습 카드"

numbers:prompt.findIncorrectExpression.why: was 어느 쪽이 맞을까요? — which one is right? — over an option list whose answer is the one that is wrong

numbers:prompt.meaning.definition.why: 무슨 뜻일까요?를 대신한다. 정의를 묻는 자리에서만 쓰이므로 "무엇을 나타낼까요"가 정확하다.

numbers:prompt.meaning.moneyAmount.why: 가격 네 개를 놓고 "무슨 뜻일까요?"라고 물으면 정의를 묻는 것처럼 읽힌다. 금액을 묻는 자리이므로 "얼마"를 쓴다.

numbers:prompt.meaning.clockTime.why: 시각을 묻는 자리. 한국어로 시각을 묻는 가장 자연스러운 말이 "몇 시일까요?"다.

numbers:prompt.meaning.month.why: 월을 묻는 자리. "몇 월"이 관용이며 "무슨 월"은 쓰지 않는다.
